newsitem.title: UK: Brazil, South Africa cited in sugar freight orders.
newsitem.headline: Brazil, South Africa cited in sugar freight orders.

text.p: London's sugar freight market saw a spate of fresh inquiry on Monday with Brazil and South Africa cited as the most significant quoted origins for new business.

Shipbrokers said Cargill was engaged in nominating a number of vessels to ship sugar from Brazil, adding that this could be connected to last week's hefty delivery against New York's May futures contract.
They said the 29,000 dwt Ailsa, built in 1972, was fixed for a prompt order but gave no further details.
Cargill also quoted for 14/25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Paranagua or Santos to the Egyptian Med, Black Sea or Baltic for prompt shipment dates.
As a result of its recent selling tender, South Africa Sugar Association (SASA) fixed 18,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Durban to Toronto for May 21/28.
Andre fixed 7/10,000 tonnes from Djibouti to east Africa for prompt dates, with Berbera-Dar es Salaam cited as the destination range.
Finagrain was said to have fixed 5/10,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from east coast Mexico to west Africa for May 8/15.

Pacol's fixture of 23,000 tonnes of bulk sugar, reported last week, from Cuba to the Black Sea for prompt shipment achieved a rate of $28.50. The name of the vessel has yet to emerge, market sources said.

Other new business included Jean Lion, which was open for 14,000 tonnes in bags from Antwerp to Umm Qasr for 14 days notice and Genoc, which quoted for a prompt 14,000 tonnes from Thailand to Pakistan.
E D & F Man quoted for 12,600/15,400 tonnes from Puerto Quetzal to Algeria for mid-May and a further 5/6,000 tonnes in bags from Santander to west Africa for the second half of May.
Kerry was open for a 14,000-tonne bulk cargo from Thailand to south China for mid-May, while Louis Dreyfus quoted for 5,000 tonnes in bags from Thailand to Maputo for similar dates.
Lastly, Czarnikow-Rionda was open for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from south Brazil to east or west Africa.
In other news, Colombia's largest truck drivers' organisation is to meet transport ministry officials at 1900 GMT in a bid to avert a nationwide strike.
Pakistan bought one cargo of white sugar at the end of last week but the shipment period has yet to emerge.

On Monday, Pakistan said it would decide on Wednesday the result of a tender to buy 50,000 tonnes of crystal whites, to reach Karachi in two equal shipments by June 20 and July 10. The tender was opened on Saturday.
